subject.title: Cron Jobs Calendar View for Control UI

question: Should OpenClaw accept a repaired 24-hour Cron Jobs timeline as the first Control UI product slice, or require a broader daily/week/calendar design before implementation?
rationale: This is not a broken existing contract; it is a Control UI product-scope choice, and the open implementation PR covers only part of the requested calendar/timeline surface while crossing current UI architecture and cron status contracts.

options.title: Repair Narrow Timeline First
options.body: Rebase and fix the linked PR or a replacement against the current cron page, preserve existing cron contracts, and treat the 24-hour timeline as an intentional first slice.

options.title: Design Full Calendar Scope
options.body: Pause implementation until maintainers define daily, weekly, quick-stats, drag-and-drop, and validation behavior together.

options.title: Decline Core Calendar View
options.body: Close the issue and linked PR after documenting that the current list and run-history UI is sufficient for core.

recommendation.title: Repair Narrow Timeline First
recommendation.body: Rebase and fix the linked PR or a replacement against the current cron page, preserve existing cron contracts, and treat the 24-hour timeline as an intentional first slice.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Control UI product-surface and docs history makes this the strongest available routing signal for the product-scope decision.
